recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. Treat FHIR-3701 as historically applied for DSTU1 and superseded by later Condition Patient|Group modeling; require a new current-version Patient Care decision before changing the element name again.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive with Modification Patient Care issue requesting Condition.subject be renamed to Condition.patient because Condition was then only allowed to reference Patient; Jira records approval of the change and cites svn revision 4796.
initial_application: Git commit 925a359a770f79cf932102b21172cd2b36fc1f00, '#3701 - rename Condition.subject to patient', applied the request by renaming Condition examples and the then-current spreadsheet definition from subject to patient.
additional_context: Current source/fhir.ini keeps Condition in the build, and source/condition/structuredefinition-Condition.xml defines Condition.subject as Reference(Patient|Group) with alias patient. Later Published issue FHIR-11089 explicitly resolved that Condition can be Patient or Group, so subject is correct. Git commit e35d3b3f92f11757466373e8b8f9f829d96d5cc9 reworked Condition to the Patient|Group subject model. Related search-parameter issues FHIR-6094 and FHIR-8142 are already represented on the combined branch as no-change audits for the same superseded patient/subject history.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-renaming current Condition.subject to Condition.patient would contradict the active Patient|Group model and the later Patient Care decision.

related_jiras.note: Later Published Patient Care decision says AllergyIntolerance.patient is correct because AllergyIntolerance is only Patient, while Condition can be Patient or Group so Condition.subject is correct.
Related 2015 Condition subject-to-patient search-parameter rename was valid in the old model and already has a no-change audit on the combined branch because the current subject model supersedes it.
DAF ballot issue with the same Condition patient/subject search-parameter concern is already audited on the combined branch as superseded by the current subject model.
Later search-parameter work supports retaining Patient-only patient search parameters distinct from broader subject references.
